title: Access Context
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: The per-request access context: the bag a rule's `$` paths read, the caller's roles and permissions, and the gated handle bound to that bag.

axioms.text: The [[access context]] is built once per request, by the app's hydration middleware, and every layer below reads it.
The engine takes permissions and a bag on every call. It never reads the database to find out who is asking.
Every value in the bag is trusted. Building it from server-side sources is the app's job.

purpose.intro: What a rule can say about the caller is whatever the bag holds. This page is the bag's shape, the context around it, and how a `$` path resolves.
purpose.note: `ScopedAcRequestContext` is the one place the library names the app's session shape, a named exception to AC37 in [[access-control|Access Control]]. The engine and the gate still take the bag as `unknown`.

reference.statement: `src/context.ts` declares the context and its bag. Every slice and app imports them from `@libs/gated-scoped-ac`.

claims.text: `bag`: the subjects the rules read, passed to every engine call.
`roles`: the baseline roles plus the active organization's membership roles, resolved on the server.
`permissions`: the permissions those roles carry, resolved once by `engine.resolveEffectivePermissions(roles, bag)`. This, not `roles`, is what the engine's calls take.
`gateDb`: the [[gated db]] bound to this bag, the only path to the database for scoped work.

reference.statement: A `$` path is walked through the bag: `$session.user.id` reads `bag.session.user.id`.

claims.text: `$session.organization.id`, `$session.organization.type`: the active organization, or `null` when none is active. The type is also where the engine looks for the forest to use (`orgTypePath`, default `$session.organization.type`).

`$requestBody.*`: the row being created. The gate's `create` sets it to the values it inserts, replacing whatever the caller put there. A service that wants an early `allowCreate` verdict adds it to a copy of the bag itself.

A path that is not set, or set to null, is absent, and every condition reading it fails, negations included. The engine has no list of valid paths, so a rule naming a path the bag never holds loads fine and then never matches. See [[gated-scoped-ac-security|Security]].

reference.statement: The app's hydration middleware runs after the session is verified and before any route, and builds the context only for a signed-in request.

claims.text: It reads the active organization from the session, already checked against the caller's memberships, and never from anything the client asserts.
It unions the baseline roles (the roots of `accountBaseline`) with the active membership's roles, calls `resolveEffectivePermissions` once, and binds a `gateDb` to the bag.
An unauthenticated request gets no context and passes through: hydration never rejects. A route that needs one answers 401 when it is missing.

In this repo the middleware is `buildScopedAc` in `apps/main/slices/seed/user-organization-mgmt/api/middlewares/create-scoped-ac-middleware.ts`, and open-api builds the same shape for a delegated user. See [[gated-scoped-ac-mount|Mount]].

reference.statement: A slice never builds the context; it reads the one hydration stored on the request.

claims.text: A slice's Hono env declares `scopedAc?: ScopedAcRequestContext`; its route helper reads it and answers 401 when it is absent.
Services take the context as their first argument and pass `ac.permissions` and `ac.bag` to the engine, and `ac.gateDb` (or a `gatedDb(bag)` of their own, for a bag they extended) to the repository.
